android_mechanism: Packet-factory properties cache grows without bound; fix bounds the retained data
bug_description: The home article list is bound to PersistentStorage ('homeList'). Every load-more during infinite scrolling concatenates another page and rewrites the ENTIRE accumulated list (JSON serialization + preferences write) to disk, so persistent-storage write time and retained memory grow quadratically with scroll depth; the full tail is also re-parsed on every cold start even though it is stale feed data.
fix_summary: Only the first-page home-article snapshot is persisted ('homeListCache') for fast cold-start rendering; pages loaded during the session accumulate in component state without rewriting persistent storage.
trigger_steps: Install and launch the app with network access.
Start hitrace capture (categories: app, sched, disk, filesystem).
Scroll the home list to trigger at least 10 load-more cycles (200+ accumulated items).
Stop hitrace; also record app memory (hdc shell hidumper -s 1909 -a '-mem' or similar). Repeat 3 repetitions for unfixed, then install fixed and repeat 3 repetitions.

test_oracle.definition: Bytes written to app preferences/storage attributable to home-list persistence per load-more cycle, from disk/filesystem trace activity (write sizes grow with list length in unfixed, stay constant in fixed).
test_oracle.comparison: unfixed: write size per load-more grows linearly with accumulated pages (total write volume quadratic in pages); fixed: writes only at first-page fetch. unfixed_total_write_bytes > fixed by >= 3x after 10 pages; unfixed resident memory higher.

trace_config.command: hdc shell hitrace --time 60 app sched disk filesystem -o /data/local/tmp/wan_persist.chtrace
